body: Same answer as VectorCraft and AvoidMissingBall. A PR adds no check we lack: `cargo xtask land` gates every commit, waits for the whole-branch Codex review and refuses unresolved findings, and pre-push refuses any commit without a clean review (plus gitleaks). We have no CI to run on a PR. The cost would be a GitHub round trip per landing (we land 10+ branches a day through one land slot), with the review kept in two places. What PRs would give you: a page per branch to read and comment on. If you want that, VectorCraft's cheap form works for us too: `xtask land` opens a read-only PR with the review pasted in and closes it when it fast-forwards main. We'd switch at the same time as the other two.
summary: BewareILive on PRs: stay on fast-forward, same as both sisters; switch all three together only if you want to read diffs on GitHub
